DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http://v.wu.dilg.com.ph MR. PRIMO ARTHUR J. CORDETA Blk 3, Lot 69, Quirino St. Villa San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan Dear Mr. Cordeta: This has reference to your letter dated 23 September 2019 concerning your application for retirement benefits at the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP). Per your letter and its attachment, you had rendered service as Sangguniang Barangay Member for six (6) years- from 1989 to 1994. Thereafter, you were employed at the BFP from 1995 to 2003, as shown in the attached Service Record. You applied for retirement benefits before the BFP requesting that the number of years you rendered as Sangguniang Barangay Member be tacked to your service at the BFP in order to avail your retirement benefits. Ostensibly, the BFP National Headquarter did not grant your request. Hence, your letter-request that your six (6) years of service as Sangguniang Barangay Member be credited as part of your service at the BFP in order to avail your retirement benefits. Foremost, under Republic Act No. 6975, otherwise known as the Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1990, retirement among uniformed personnel, such as the BFP, can be done through compulsory and optional. Sections 39 and 40 thereof respectively provide, thusly: "SECTION 39. Compulsory Retirement. — Compulsory retirement, for officer and non-officer, shall be upon the attainment of age fifty-six (56): Provided, That, in case of any officer with the rank of chief superintendent, director or deputy director general, the

Commission may allow his retention in the service for an unextendible period of one (1) year. SECTION 40. Optional Retirement. — Upon accumulation of at least twenty (20) years of satisfactory active service, an officer or non-officer, at his own request and with the approval of the Commission, shall be retired from the service and entitled to receive benefits provided for by law." We are of the understanding that you opted for optional retirement as herein issue concerns the length of years rendered at the BFP to avail retirement benefits. On this, attention is invited to Section 40 of RA 6975, as above-cited, thus: "Optional Retirement. — Upon accumulation of at least twenty (20) years of satisfactory active service, an officer or non-officer, at his own request and with the approval of the Commission, shall be retired from the service and entitled to receive benefits provided for by law." (Emphasis supplied) As can be discerned from the foregoing, BFP personnel may opt for optional retirement upon the accumulation of twenty (20) years of service and be entitled to receive benefits provided by law. Perusal of the attached Service Record, it appears that you had rendered less than twenty (20) years of service at the BFP. However, it is noteworthy to mention that the twenty- year service requirement is not necessarily a service rendered at the BFP. Section 72 of the same Act defined "active service" as: "SECTION 72. Active Service. — For purposes of this Act, active service of the uniformed personnel shall refer to services rendered as an officer and non-officer, cadet, trainee or draftee in the PNP, Fire or Jail Force or in the municipal police prior to the integration of the PC-INP or in the AFP, and services rendered as a civilian official or employee in the Philippine Government prior to the date of separation or retirement from the PNP, Fire or Jail Force: Provided, That, for purposes of retirement he shall have rendered at least ten (10) years of active service as officer or non-officer in the AFP, and lor in the INP and/or in the PNP, Fire or Jail Force: Provided, further, That services rendered as cadet, probationary officer, trainee or draftee in the AFP or as cadet or trainee in the INP and PNP shall be credited for purposes of longevity pay: Provided, finally, That, for cadet services, the maximum number of

service to be credited shall not exceed the duration of the pre- commissionship course specified in the curriculum." It is equally noteworthy to mention that the abovequoted provision specifically provides that for purposes of retirement a BFP personnel shall have rendered at least ten (10) years of active service as officer or non- officer in the BFP. Accordingly, we are of the view that the number of years you had rendered as Sangguniang Barangay Member cannot be incorporated to the length of your service at the BFP to satisfy the required years of service, as above-cited. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: SEC. E O ubli Safety DIRECTOR JOSE S.
